Present Perfect When Commenting on the Present Results of Something in the Past
You use the Present Perfect to talk about past actions that have a connection to the present.
When you want to comment on the present results of a past action you can use the Present Perfect with verbs like appear, seem and sound.
For example:

It sounds as if you've already decided on the next course of action.
It seems they have completed the report ahead of schedule.
The form of the Present Perfect is:
subject + has/have + past participle
You can use since and yet to introduce the past event.

• Since the beginning of their friendship they have tried all sorts of solutions.
  • Yet, no matter what they try, their prickly problem has remained.
Since there has been a lot of talk of late about sadness and conflict, a book about hugs seems like a perfect subject to read during the holiday season.
Since the beginning of their friendship they have tried all sorts of solutions.

How to write a review of a book

When you a review a book, you are offering a combination of summary and commentary on what you have read.
You are also trying to persuade the reader.
Book reviews are written in formal language and in paragraphs.
Here are the general elements of a book review:

Introduction

You need to provide basic information about the book:

• Title and the author
  • Publication Information
  • Genre
  • A brief introduction to the book and the review
Body
Provide brief descriptions of the setting and other major characters.
Explain the plot.
How would you describe the writing style?
Are there images or illustrations? How do they connect to the text?
Be careful not to give away important plot details or the ending.

You can write about your own opinions.
Would you recommend it to others? Why or why not?
Conclusion
Briefly conclude by pulling your thoughts together. You may want to say what impression the book left you with, or emphasize what you want your reader to know about it.

images.text: When I went for a neighborhood stroll with a publisher friend of mine, she handed me a copy of the delightfully engaging, Winnie's World to take home and enjoy. I couldn't resist publishing a review online about my reactions to the children's book that very evening. Since there has been a lot of talk of late about sadness, conflict and negativity related to social media, a book about hugs and connecting with others seems like a perfect subject to read during the holiday season. Winnie and Wally are the very best of friends. They love to play in the park together, make yummy cakes together and even go on holidays with their families together. However, there is one thing that these little hedgehogs can't do and that is hug each other because of their pesky prickles. Since the beginning of their friendship they have tried all sorts of solutions. Yet, no matter what they try, their prickly problem has remained. They have even considered wrapping themselves in tissue paper until their long lost relative has a solution!

Written and illustrated by Canadian husband and wife team Marisa Mitchell (author) and Ronald Atkins (illustrator), Winnie's World is a charming picture book, ideal for bedtime. It's excellent for encouraging conversations about family, friendship, sharing and patience. It is also ideal for providing an introductory explanation of different personalities and the sharing of personal information over the internet.

Atkin's illustrations are simply breathtaking. Children and adults alike are in for a visual treat. He offers the reader images that leap from the page and incredible attention to detail. The text is simple, talking about all the things Winnie and Wally do together, as well as their attempts to safely give each other a friendly hug. Since the official release of Winnie's World has not yet happened, it is a good idea to place orders now. It is the perfect book for the holiday season and to slip into a Christmas stocking. It's also great for reading as you could cuddle up with your child during the festive season. This children's book is the most recent offering by BFP Publishing and solidifies their position in providing high-quality literature to their readership. Look out for it in early December.
